title: Open Source AI Without the FOMO
subtitle: From model evaluation to deployment, in plain words
intro: New open-source AI models drop every week. The State of Open Source AI (2023) ebook calls it a fast-paced mess — and offers clarity from evaluation to deployment.
takeaway: Open-source AI gives you shared models to evaluate and deploy, but you must check quality and run it yourself.

sections.heading: Analogy: a community recipe book
sections.body:
Think of open-source AI like a public recipe book. Anyone can copy a recipe (a model), taste-test it, and improve it.

A model is the learned recipe. Evaluation is the taste test. Deployment is serving it in your own kitchen. Open-source licensing means you can use and share it freely.

This sharing is why it exists, as you'll see next.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: clarity in the chaos
sections.body:
Closed AI keeps the recipe secret. Open-source AI publishes it so you can inspect, compare, and build on it.

The ebook from premAI-io guides you from model evaluations (how good is it?) to deployment (how to run it for users). That helps you cure FOMO and pick what fits.

But sharing freely also creates risks, which is what can go wrong.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when sharing breaks
sections.body:
A public recipe can be untested, outdated, or unsafe. A model might score well in evaluation but fail in your deployment.

You also take on the work: hosting, updates, and checking the license (like CC-BY-4.0 or Apache-2.0). If you skip evaluation, you serve a bad dish to users.

steps.narration: Someone shares a trained model openly.
You evaluate it on your task.
You share fixes back to the community.

quiz.q: What does 'model evaluation' mean in open-source AI?
options: Writing a license for the model
Testing how well a model performs before using it
quiz.why: Evaluation is the taste-test to compare models before you deploy.

quiz.q: Why does open-source AI exist according to the ebook?
options: To provide clarity and shared building blocks from evaluation to deployment
To stop anyone from deploying models
To replace all closed models overnight
quiz.why: It offers an overview from evaluation to deployment to navigate fast innovation together.

quiz.q: What breaks first if you deploy an open model without evaluation?
options: You may serve bad or unsafe answers to users
quiz.why: Skipping evaluation means you miss failures that only show up on your data.
